frozen: 2026-10-23, after plan 1 (growing-season reliability) was rejected and before any plan 2 result
plan1_result: No growing-season setting beat none on the mean of the HYDE 200 CE and Han ranks (best 0.762 vs 0.794): HYDE rose 0.746 -> 0.758-0.779 but Han fell 0.843 -> 0.28-0.77.
finding: Split by temperature and dryness (Old World 15-50 N, away from rivers), the settlement base over HYDE is: cool (mean annual <= 8 C) and dry 2.2-3.7x; cool and moist 1.1-3.0x; warm and dry with 30-120 growing days 1.3-1.8x; warm with 120-180 days 0.6-0.7x. The short-season excess is mostly a cold-margin one (Tibet, Mongolia, the high plateaus), with a smaller dry-margin part.
hypothesis: Low-input harvests on the margins are worth less than their mean: frost and a short frost-free season on cold land, failed rains on dry land. Crop capacity x R_cold x R_dry, R_cold = clip((T_ann - t0) / (t1 - t0), 0, 1), R_dry = clip((P/PET - a0) / (a1 - a0), 0, 1); irrigated land keeps its harvest from the dry factor (max with irrigation access); grazing is unchanged.
fitting: as plan 1: the highest mean of the HYDE 200 CE and Han AD 2 ranks for the full model (old cores, travel cost, L 800 km); ties within 0.005 go to fewer factors, then the milder setting
held_out: Roman towns AD 150 and the great cities of AD 100-200, once, for the chosen setting against none
